GNAQ/GNA11 signaling pathway

GNAQ/GNA11 signaling pathway. ① Ligand binding and ARF6 activation: when the ligand binds to CysLTR2, GNAQ/GNA11, and the ARF-guanine nucleotide exchange factor GEP100 coactivate ARF6. This interaction redistributes GNAQ/GNA11 from the cell surface to active signaling vesicles in the cytoplasm, initiating subsequent signaling pathways [61]. GNAQ/GNA11 activates PLCB4, which hydrolyzes PIP2 to generate the second messengers IP3 and DAG. DAG binds to PKC and Ras, leading to the sequential phosphorylation of Ras, Raf, MAPK, and other downstream signaling molecules. These signals are then transmitted to the nucleus to regulate gene expression and induce UM. ② Rho/Rac GTPase pathway: GNAQ/GNA11 directly binds to Trio-mediated Rho/Rac GTPases [69]. Activated ARF6 can also induce the Rho/Rac signaling pathway directly [61]. This activation leads to the downstream activation of FAK, which subsequently activates YAP via MOB1. Additionally, activation of Rho/Rac GTPases stimulates F-actin, further activating YAP. Ultimately, this process triggers YAP/TEAD-mediated transcription [70]. ③ β-catenin pathway: oncogenic GNAQ/GNA11 activation of ARF6 leads to the release of β-catenin from the plasma membrane and its translocation to the nucleus. In the nucleus, β-catenin induces gene transcription and promotes UM cell proliferation [61,64]. ④ PI3K/AKT pathway: although not directly controlled by GNAQ/GNA11, activation of the PI3K/AKT pathway can also induce UM [71,72]. ARF6, ADP-ribosylation factor; GEP, gene expression profiling; UM, uveal melanoma
